lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to World 24, the Cloudtop Railway! Do you remember the silver ticket from the Sleeping Seed? Today, we climb the stairs to the roof of the lab. Look! There's a little station on the roof, and a long white train. This train runs above the clouds! Say it with me. This train runs above the clouds! Wonderful! Runs means goes. Most trains run on tracks, but this train runs on clouds. Let's read the sign on the platform. "Welcome to Rooftop Station! The Cloud Train runs above the clouds from here to Cloud Junction. The train leaves every morning at nine. Please show your ticket to the conductor. Stand behind the yellow line. Enjoy your trip!" What time does the train leave? At nine. Where do you stand? Behind the yellow line. Good. Listen! The conductor is calling. All aboard! The train is leaving. Now, phonics. In this world, we'll say place names the English way. Canada. America. Italy. Mexico. In English, one part is strong. CAN-a-da. a-MER-i-ca. IT-a-ly. MEX-i-co. Now, let's find our seats!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're at Cloud Junction. It's a very big station with lots of trains. Our silver tickets were only for the first ride, so now we need new tickets to the last stop, Star Station. Let's go to the ticket office. What do we say? A ticket to Star Station, please. Say it with me. A ticket to Star Station, please. Great! Then ask, How much is it? Let's read the price board next to the window. "Cloudtop Railway Prices. Cloud Junction to Rainbow Falls: 4 coins. To Mist Mountain: 6 coins. To Moon Lake: 7 coins. To Star Station: 8 coins. Children under twelve pay half price." How much is a ticket to Star Station? Eight coins. But children pay half. Half of eight is four. So you pay four coins! When the clerk gives you the ticket, they say, Here you are. Have a nice trip! Now, phonics. Osaka. Hokkaido. Korea. Okinawa. In Japanese, we say these names flat. In English, one part is strong. o-SA-ka. hok-KAI-do. ko-RE-a. o-ki-NA-wa. Let's buy our tickets!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! At the ticket office, the clerk often asks a question. One way or round trip? What does that mean? One way means you go there, and you don't come back. Round trip (おうふく) means you go there and come back. If you want to come back, say, Round trip, please. Let's practice. One way or round trip? Round trip, please. Say it with me. One way or round trip? Round trip, please. Excellent! Here is a ticket. Let's read it together. "Cloudtop Railway. From: Cloud Junction. To: Moon Lake. Round trip. Adults: 1. Children: 4. You can use this ticket for seven days. Please keep it until the end of your trip." Is it one way or round trip? Round trip. How many children? Four. Good reading! But our trip ends at Star Station, so we need one-way tickets. Now, phonics. Africa. Australia. Nagasaki. India. AF-ri-ca. aus-TRA-li-a. na-ga-SA-ki. IN-di-a. Can you hear the strong part? Let's choose our tickets!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Cloud Junction has twelve platforms. Which one is ours? When you don't know, look at the departure board, or ask. Which platform does the train leave from? Say it with me. Which platform does the train leave from? Great! The answer is, It leaves from platform 3. Let's read the departure board. "Departures. 10:15 Cloud Express to Star Station, platform 3. 10:30 Rainbow Line to Rainbow Falls, platform 5. 10:45 Mist Line to Mist Mountain, platform 1. Please check this board before you go to the platform." Which platform does the Cloud Express leave from? Platform 3. What time does the Rainbow Line leave? At 10:30. Good job! If you're not sure, ask the station staff. Excuse me. Is this the right platform for Star Station? Now, phonics. Singapore. Antarctica. Argentina. Portugal. SIN-ga-pore. ant-ARC-ti-ca. ar-gen-TI-na. POR-tu-gal. Clap on the strong part. Remember, the board can change, so check it again before the train comes. And platform 3 is up the stairs, so walk. Don't run! Let's find the right platform!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, you are the station staff at Cloud Junction! Station staff help travelers. First, say hello. Welcome to Cloud Junction! How can I help you? Then, answer questions about trains. The next train leaves at 10:15 from platform 3. Say it with me. The next train leaves at 10:15 from platform 3. Perfect! Station staff also make announcements. Let's read this morning's announcement. "Good morning, everyone. The next train to Star Station leaves at 10:15 from platform 3. The train to Rainbow Falls leaves at 10:30 from platform 5. Please don't run on the platform. Thank you for riding the Cloudtop Railway." Read it again in a clear, slow voice, like real staff. Great! Remember the words for tickets, too. A ticket to Star Station, please. One way or round trip? Which platform? Now, phonics review. Canada. Okinawa. Australia. Argentina. Hokkaido. CAN-a-da. o-ki-NA-wa. aus-TRA-li-a. ar-gen-TI-na. hok-KAI-do. Good station staff speak clearly and kindly. Look at the traveler, smile and use a polite voice. Let's open our station!

phonics.tipJa: have の あとは 3つめの かたち。see → saw → seen、be → was → been、do → did → done、go → went → gone。seen は「イーン」と ながく、been は アメリカでは「ビン」と みじかく、done は「ダン」、gone は「ゴーン」と よむよ。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're on the Cloud Express now. Today, we'll learn how to ask about experiences. An experience is something you did in your life. Have you ever seen a rainbow? Have you ever seen a shooting star? Have you ever means, at any time in your life. Today's question is, Have you ever seen a rainbow train? Say it with me. Have you ever seen a rainbow train? Wonderful! The answer is, Yes, I have. Or no, I haven't. Look, there's a magazine in the seat pocket. Let's read it. "The Rainbow Train runs only once a month. It has seven cars, and each car is a different color. Many people want to see it, but only a few people have seen it. Some people say it brings good luck." How often does it run? Once a month. How many cars does it have? Seven. After you say Yes, I have, tell us more. Yes, I have. I saw it ten years ago. Now, phonics. Seen. Been. Done. Gone. See, saw, seen. Be, was, been. Do, did, done. Go, went, gone. After have, use seen. Keep your eyes on the window!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Have you ever seen a rainbow train? Today, we'll talk about places. When you went to a place in the past, you can say, I've been to Hokkaido. I've means I have. Say it with me. I've been to Hokkaido. Great! Ask your friend, Have you ever been to Okinawa? Then, a good listener asks more questions. When did you go? How was it? Let's read a page from Riko's travel notebook. "Places I've been to: Hokkaido, Kyoto and Okinawa. My favorite was Hokkaido. I went there last winter with my family. We saw lots of snow, and we ate hot ramen. Places I want to go to: Canada and Australia." Where has Riko been? Hokkaido, Kyoto and Okinawa. When did she go to Hokkaido? Last winter. Look carefully. For the experience, we say, I've been to. For the time, we say, I went there last winter. Now, phonics. Eaten. Taken. Given. Spoken. Eat, ate, eaten. Take, took, taken. Give, gave, given. Speak, spoke, spoken. Let's share our trips!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Listen. Snacks! Drinks! Here comes the snack cart. On a train, you can buy food from a cart. But what are these? I've never eaten them! When you have no experience, say, I've never. Say it with me. I've never eaten it. Is it good? Wonderful! Never means not even one time. Let's read the menu on the cart. "Cloud Cart Snacks. Cloud bun: soft and sweet, like a real cloud. 2 coins. Thunder chips: spicy and crunchy! 1 coin. Moon milk: warm milk with honey. 2 coins. Rainbow jelly: seven flavors in one cup. 3 coins." Which snack is spicy? Thunder chips. Which snack is like a cloud? The cloud bun. Have you ever tried thunder chips? You can answer, No, never. Or no, I've never tried them. Here, try means eat something new. Now, phonics. Written. Ridden. Forgotten. Hidden. Write, wrote, written. Ride, rode, ridden. The middle sound is short, so we double the letter. Let's try something new!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, Conductor Nimbus showed us his old notebook. He's a tall bird with a blue hat, and he loves this train. Let's read it. "Conductor Nimbus's Notebook. I started working on this train thirty years ago. I've crossed the Cloud Bridge more than a thousand times. I've seen the Rainbow Train fifty times. But I've never been to the Cave of Riddles. Maybe someday!" How many times has he seen the Rainbow Train? Fifty times! When we count experiences, we say, once, twice, three times, four times. One time is once. Two times is twice. Say it with me. I've been there twice. Excellent! To ask, say, How many times have you been to the sea? You can answer, Once. Twice. Many times. Or I've never been there. Now, phonics. Flown. Drawn. Grown. Swum. Fly, flew, flown. Draw, drew, drawn. Grow, grew, grown. Swim, swam, swum. How many times have you swum in the sea? Let's count our experiences!

phonics.tipJa: 過去分詞の まとめ: see → saw → seen、go → went → gone、eat → ate → eaten、write → wrote → written（t を 2つ）、fly → flew → flown。have の あとは いつも 3つめの かたち！

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! This is our 700th lesson! Congratulations! You've come so far. Let's celebrate with Experience Bingo! Here's your bingo card. Ask your friends the questions. If your friend says, Yes, I have, write their name in the box. Let's read the card. "Experience Bingo. Ask your friends! Have you ever ridden a horse? Have you ever eaten curry for breakfast? Have you ever seen a shooting star? Have you ever swum in the sea? Have you ever flown in a plane?" Let's practice the first question. Have you ever ridden a horse? Say it with me. Have you ever ridden a horse? Great! When you say Yes, I have, add one more thing. Yes, I have. I rode one at a farm. When? Where? How was it? If you get five in a row, shout, Bingo! I got five in a row! Now, phonics review. Seen. Gone. Eaten. Written. Flown. See, saw, seen. Go, went, gone. Eat, ate, eaten. Write, wrote, written. Fly, flew, flown. Ready? Let's play!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we're at Sky Harbor. It's the biggest station on the Cloudtop Railway. There are twenty platforms and lots of people. Oh no! Where's Birimo? He was lost for a few minutes! But he did the right thing. He went to the information desk and said, Excuse me. I'm lost. Could you help me? Say it with me. Excuse me. I'm lost. Could you help me? Very good! Look, there's a poster on the wall. Let's read it. "Lost at the station? Don't worry! 1. Stay calm. 2. Look for station staff in blue uniforms. 3. Go to the information desk. 4. Don't go anywhere with strangers. 5. Tell the staff your group's meeting place." Who can help you? Station staff in blue uniforms. Should you go anywhere with strangers? No! The staff will ask, Where do you want to go? You can answer, I want to go to the Rainbow Line. Now, phonics. I've. You've. We've. They've. I have becomes I've. We have becomes we've. Bite your lip softly for the v. Stay calm, and ask for help!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're still at Sky Harbor. Haru went to buy snacks for everyone. But when he came back, the train doors closed! The train left without us. Oh no! We missed the train. Say it with me. I missed the train! When's the next one? Good! When's means when is. Don't worry. Let's look at the schedule. "Rainbow Line Schedule. Sky Harbor to Rainbow Falls. 11:00, 11:20, 11:40, 12:00. Trains come every twenty minutes. The ride to Rainbow Falls is thirty minutes long." Which train did we miss? The 11:00 train. When's the next one? At 11:20. So, the next one comes in twenty minutes. In twenty minutes means twenty minutes from now. We haven't lost much time. We just have to wait. Missing a train can happen to anyone, so stay calm. Let's wait on the bench. Now, phonics. Haven't. Hasn't. I've. They've. Have not becomes haven't. Has not becomes hasn't. The mark goes between n and t. Next time, let's stay together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We arrived at Rainbow Falls. But Kiko looks worried. Her small blue bag is gone. She left it on the train! Say it with me. I left my bag on the train. Good. Left is the past of leave. Where can we go? The lost and found (わすれもの センター). People bring lost things there. Let's go to the lost and found. Look, the staff gave us a form. Let's read it. "Lost and Found. What did you lose? Which train were you on? Which car did you sit in? What does it look like? Please wait here. We'll call the train." Which train were you on, Kiko? The 11:20 train to Rainbow Falls. Which car? Car 4. Good. Kiko answered every question. The staff will call the train. Has anyone found it yet? Not yet. Let's wait and hope. Now, phonics. She's. He's. It's. Who's. Usually, she's means she is. But in she's been, it means she has. Who's seen my bag? Who has seen my bag? Let's cross our fingers for Kiko!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Good news! The staff found two blue bags on the train. But which one is Kiko's? The staff asked, What does it look like? This question means, Tell me about its size, color and shape. Kiko said, It's a small blue bag with a star on it. Say it with me. It's a small blue bag with a star on it. Great! The order is size, then color, then the thing. With a star on it tells us one special thing. Let's read the list of lost items. "Today's Lost Items. 1. A big blue bag with a red flower on it. Found in car 2. 2. A small blue bag with a star on it. Found in car 4. 3. A black umbrella. Found on platform 3. 4. A green hat with a feather. Found in the dining car." Which one is Kiko's? Number 2! The staff asked one more question to check. What's inside? My notebook and a camera. Now, phonics. We've. Hasn't. She's. It's. We have, has not, she has, it has. Let's describe our things!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! On this trip, people helped us many times. Today, it's our turn to help other people. Let's read the Station Helper Card. "Station Helper Card. If someone looks worried: 1. Say, Are you OK? 2. Listen carefully. 3. Say, Don't worry. I'll help you. 4. Find the station staff or your grown-up. Never go anywhere alone with a stranger." First, we ask, Are you OK? You look worried. Then, we listen. Then, we say, Don't worry. I'll help you. Say it with me. Don't worry. I'll help you. Wonderful! You are kind helpers. But remember, children help by finding an adult. Let's ask the station staff together. Today, Birimo will be a traveler with a problem. Can you help him? Use the words from our trip. I'm lost. I missed the train. I left my bag on the train. It's a small blue bag. Now, phonics review. I've. Haven't. Who's. It's. Taken. Who's taken my ticket? Who has taken my ticket? Let's be station helpers!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! The train is climbing up, up, up. Let's go to the observation car. It's the best car for looking outside. Wow! When something is really amazing, we say, What a view! Say it with me. What a view! I can see the mountains. Wonderful! You can use What a with other things, too. What a beautiful lake! What a big waterfall! What a long bridge! Here's a page from the train guidebook. Let's read it. "The Observation Car. This car has glass walls and a glass roof. From here, you can see Mist Mountain, Moon Lake and the Cloud Sea. The best view is at the top of the Cloud Bridge. Don't forget your camera!" What can you see from the observation car? Mist Mountain, Moon Lake and the Cloud Sea. Where is the best view? At the top of the Cloud Bridge. Now, phonics. Overlook. Overpass. Overflow. Overtake. Over means above or across. The station overlooks the valley. It's up high, and you can see everything below. What a view!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! The train is passing Rainbow Falls Valley. There's so much to see! Today, we'll describe the view, like a picture. First, say what you see. Look out the window! There's a castle. Say it with me. Look out the window! There's a castle. Great! Then, tell us where it is. On the left. On the right. On top of a hill. Next to the castle. Under the waterfall. In front of the castle. Riko bought a postcard of this view. Let's read the back of it. "A postcard from Rainbow Falls. On the left, there's an old castle on top of a hill. On the right, there's a tall waterfall. Under the waterfall, there's a small rainbow. In front of the castle, sheep are eating grass." Where is the castle? On top of a hill. What's under the waterfall? A small rainbow. When you describe a picture, move your eyes from left to right. Now, phonics. Underwater. Underline. Undersea. Underpass. Under means below. Underline the place words on the postcard. Let's describe the view!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! At Mist Mountain, many people got on the train. Now the car is crowded. Where can we sit? There's an empty seat, but maybe it's somebody's seat. So, we ask politely. Excuse me. Is this seat taken? Say it with me. Excuse me. Is this seat taken? Very polite! Taken means somebody is using it. If it's free, you'll hear, No, it isn't. Please sit down. Look, there's a sign about train manners. Let's read it. "Car 6 Manners. Please put big bags on the overhead rack. Please give your seat to older people and people with small children. Please talk quietly. Please don't put your feet on the seats." Where do big bags go? On the overhead rack. Who should we give our seats to? Older people and people with small children. If you need help with your bag, ask, Can I put my bag up there? Now, phonics. Overhead. Overcoat. Undershirt. Underground. Over means above. Under means below. Let's be polite on the train!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! It's lunchtime. Some trains have a dining car. It's like a restaurant on a train. Let's go and order lunch. To order, say, I'll have the sandwich set, please. Say it with me. I'll have the sandwich set, please. Delicious! The waiter will ask, Would you like something to drink? You can say, Orange juice, please. Let's read the menu first. "Dining Car Menu. Sandwich set: two sandwiches, soup and fruit. 6 coins. Cloud curry: mild and creamy. 7 coins. Mountain noodles: hot noodles with vegetables. 6 coins. Drinks: orange juice, apple juice, milk or tea. 2 coins." What's in the sandwich set? Two sandwiches, soup and fruit. How much is the cloud curry? Seven coins. If you need something else, ask politely. Can I have some water, please? When the food comes, say, Thank you. It looks delicious! Now, phonics. Overeat. Oversleep. Overnight. Underpass. Over can mean too much. Overeat means eat too much. Don't overeat, Haru! Let's order lunch!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! On a long train ride, you can talk with other passengers. This is called small talk. Let's read some tips. "Train Talk Tips. 1. Say hello and smile. 2. Ask an easy question: Where are you going? 3. Listen, and ask one more question: Have you ever been there? Why are you going there? 4. Say something nice at the end: That sounds fun! Have a nice trip!" Let's practice the easy question. Where are you going? I'm going to the sea. Say it with me. Where are you going? I'm going to the sea. Great! The secret of good small talk is asking one more question. If someone says, I love fishing, ask, Have you ever caught a big fish? Then, say something nice at the end. That sounds fun! Have a nice trip! And remember, talk with new people only when your family or teacher is with you. Now, phonics review. Overlook. Overtake. Underwater. Overhead. Undersea. Over is above. Under is below. Let's have some train talk!

phonics.tipJa: p で はじまる ことばの はんたいは im-。polite → impolite（しつれいな）、perfect → imperfect、patient → impatient（まちきれない）、possible → impossible（むりな）。p の まえでは くちを とじる m に なるよ。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're at Mist Mountain Station. Let's plan the rest of our trip. Here's the route map. When we plan a trip, we ask, How long does it take? Say it with me. How long does it take? It takes two hours. Great! Here, take means it needs time. Let's read the route map. "Cloudtop Railway Route Map. Rainbow Falls to Mist Mountain: 1 hour. Mist Mountain to Moon Lake: 2 hours. Moon Lake to Crystal City: overnight train, 9 hours. Crystal City to Star Station: 30 minutes by subway." How long does it take from Mist Mountain to Moon Lake? It takes two hours. And from Crystal City to Star Station? It takes about thirty minutes by subway. About means not exactly. If we leave at four, we'll arrive at Moon Lake at six. Two hours is a long time, but don't be impatient! Look out the window and enjoy the view. Now, phonics. Impolite. Imperfect. Impatient. Impossible. These words mean the opposite. Possible, impossible. Before p, we use im. Let's make our plan!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We arrived at Moon Lake at six. The lake is shining under the moon. Now, we have a special plan. We're taking the overnight train. Say it with me. We're taking the overnight train. Wonderful! Overnight means all through the night. We'll sleep on the train, and in the morning, we'll be in Crystal City. Let's read the guide in our room. "Welcome to the Moonlight Express! Your beds are in car 8. Each room has four beds, two on the top and two on the bottom. The lights go off at nine. Breakfast is at seven in the dining car. Sleep well!" How many beds are in each room? Four. What time is breakfast? At seven. Where's my bed? Which bed is mine? You're on the top bunk. A bunk is a bed on a train or in a cabin. At night, the station lights look tiny, almost invisible. Now, phonics. Invisible. Incorrect. Incomplete. Informal. Visible means you can see it. Invisible means you can't see it. Good night! See you in the morning.

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! We slept well on the Moonlight Express, and now we're in Crystal City. Today, we'll visit the Crystal Museum. How do we get there? Take the underground line to the museum. Say it with me. Take the underground line to the museum. Great! The underground line runs under the city. Some people call it the subway. It's fast and inexpensive. Let's read the directions. "How to get to the Crystal Museum: Take the Blue Line from Crystal City Station. Change trains at Crystal Square. Take the Green Line and get off at the second stop, Museum Park. Use Exit 4. The museum is in front of the exit." Where do we change trains? At Crystal Square. Which stop do we get off at? The second stop, Museum Park. Which exit? Exit 4. When you give directions, use these words. Take. Change trains at. Get off at. Use Exit 4. And stay together on the stairs. Now, phonics. Inexpensive. Imperfect. Informal. Impatient. Before p, use im. Before other letters, use in. Let's take the subway!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Crystal City is full of interesting places. Haru wants to go everywhere! But our train to Star Station leaves at four. We have only one day. So Riko said, It's impossible to see everything in one day. Say it with me. It's impossible to see everything in one day. Good! Impossible means it can't happen. So, let's choose three places. Here's the city guide. Let's read it. "Crystal City Guide. 1. Crystal Museum: big crystals from around the world. 2. Glass Tower: see the whole city from the top. 3. Rainbow Garden: flowers in seven colors. 4. Ice Palace: a castle made of ice. 5. Starlight Market: snacks and souvenirs." Which place is made of ice? The Ice Palace. Where can you see the whole city? From the Glass Tower. Now, choose your favorite. I want to go to the museum the most. Then, say why. I love crystals. Now, phonics. Impossible. Incomplete. Incorrect. Invisible. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, each team will present a travel plan for our day in Crystal City. A good plan is easy to follow. Use order words. First, then, after that, finally. And tell us the time. It takes twenty minutes. Say it with me. First, we'll take the train. It takes twenty minutes. Excellent! Let's read Kiko's plan. "Our Day Plan. First, we'll take the Blue Line to the Crystal Museum. It takes twenty minutes. Then, we'll walk to the Ice Palace. After that, we'll have lunch at Starlight Market. It's inexpensive and delicious. Finally, we'll take the subway back to the station at three thirty." What will they do first? Take the Blue Line. Where will they have lunch? At Starlight Market. What time will they go back? At three thirty. When you listen, ask a question at the end. How long does it take from the market to the station? Now, phonics review. Impossible. Informal. Overnight. Underground. Inexpensive. Let's present our plans!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We made it! We've arrived at Star Station, the last stop on the Cloudtop Railway. The station roof is made of glass. Riko wants to write a travel blog about our trip. A blog is like a diary on the internet. Let's read her first post. "Day 1: I've arrived at Star Station! The station roof is made of glass, so I can see the stars at night. Today, I visited the Crystal Museum and the Ice Palace. I've never seen so many crystals! Tomorrow, we'll explore the town. See you!" How does Riko start? Day 1: I've arrived at Star Station! Say it with me. Day 1: I've arrived at Star Station! Great! For what you did today, use the past. Today, I visited the Crystal Museum. For an amazing first time, say, I've never seen so many crystals! But stop and think before you post. Don't put your face or your school's name online. And always ask your family first. Now, phonics review. Hokkaido. Eaten. I've. Overnight. Impossible. Let's write our blogs!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Before we leave Star Station, let's buy souvenirs. A souvenir is something you buy on a trip to remember it. Many people buy souvenirs for their family. Let's read the sign in the shop. "Star Station Souvenirs. Star keychains: 3 coins. Cloud cookies, box of twelve: 5 coins. Rainbow pencils: 2 coins. Moon snow globes: 8 coins. We wrap gifts for free!" How much is a box of cloud cookies? Five coins. Which souvenir is the most expensive? The snow globe. When you decide, say, I'll buy this for my sister. Say it with me. I'll buy this for my sister. Wonderful! When you give an idea to a friend, say, How about this star keychain? And if you want the staff to wrap it, ask, Could you wrap it, please? Think about the person. My sister loves stars. My grandparents love sweets. Now, phonics review. Italy. Seen. Haven't. Underground. Invisible. I haven't seen a snow globe like this! Let's go shopping!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! There are travelers from many countries at Star Station. Today, Birimo will play Marco, a traveler from Italy. When you go to another country, you go abroad. To ask, say, Have you ever been abroad? Say it with me. Have you ever been abroad? Great! You can answer, Yes, I've been to Canada once. Or no, I haven't been abroad yet. Here's a page from Marco's travel notebook. Let's read it. "Marco's World Map. Countries I've been to: Japan, Canada, Mexico and Australia. My favorite trip was to Australia. I saw kangaroos in the wild! Next, I want to visit Argentina and Korea." How many countries has Marco been to? Four. What did he see in Australia? Kangaroos! Then ask about the future. Which country do you want to visit someday? I want to visit Italy someday. Remember, when you talk with new people, stay with your family or teacher. Now, phonics review. Canada. America. Been. We've. She's. She's been to America. Let's talk with Marco!

phonics.tipJa: ワールド24 の ふりかえり④: o・ki・NA・wa、ride → rode → ridden（d を 2つ）、fly → flew → flown、who has → who's、overlook（うえから みる）、impolite（p の まえは im）。Who's ridden a cloud train? で みんなに きいて みよう。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! This is Star Station, the last stop. We traveled a long way on the Cloudtop Railway. Say it with me. We traveled a long way on the Cloudtop Railway. Wonderful! Let's remember. A ticket to Star Station, please. Which platform? Have you ever seen a rainbow train? I've been to Hokkaido. I'm lost. Could you help me? What a view! How long does it take? Before we leave the train, Conductor Nimbus gives us a letter and an old map. Let's read the letter. "Dear travelers, thank you for riding the Cloudtop Railway. You asked for help, you helped others, and you made many friends. Here is a present: an old map. I've never been to the place on this map, but you are brave travelers. Maybe you can go there. Your friend, Conductor Nimbus." Look at the map. There's a cave with a big question mark. What is it? Now, phonics review. Okinawa. Ridden. Flown. Who's. Overlook. Impolite. Who's ridden a cloud train? We have! Let's say goodbye to the train!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to the World 24 Grand Review! Today is our travel show in the plaza in front of Star Station. Everyone will talk about their favorite part of the trip. Start with this. I've had the best trip ever! Say it with me. I've had the best trip ever! Fantastic! In this world, you learned so much. A ticket to Star Station, please. One way or round trip? Have you ever seen a rainbow train? I've been to Hokkaido. I've never eaten it. I left my bag on the train. What a view! Is this seat taken? How long does it take? It's impossible to see everything in one day. Here's the program. Let's read it. "Cloudtop Railway Travel Show. Part one: Haru, Lunch on the Train. Part two: Kiko, The Lost Blue Bag. Part three: Riko, The Rainbow Train. Part four: Birimo, My First Overnight Train. Special thanks: Conductor Nimbus." Now, phonics review. Australia. Done. Written. They've. Underwater. Incorrect. You are wonderful travelers. Let the travel show begin!

segments.subtitleEn: Big sound review! Aus, TRA, li, a. The second part is strong. Do, did, done. Write, wrote, written, with two t's. They have becomes they've. Underwater. Incorrect, not correct.

segments.say: Say it with me. Australia. Done. Written. They've. Underwater. Incorrect. And one more. I've done it!
segments.subtitleJa: いっしょに いおう。Australia、done、written、they've、underwater、incorrect。もう ひとつ。「やりとげたよ！」
segments.subtitleEn: Say it with me. Australia. Done. Written. They've. Underwater. Incorrect. And one more. I've done it!

segments.say: Show time! Hold up your travel poster. Now, ride the train. Arms around. Choo-choo!
segments.subtitleJa: ショーの じかん！ たびの ポスターを かかげて。こんどは れっしゃに のって。うでを まわして。シュッシュッ！
segments.subtitleEn: Show time! Hold up your travel poster. Now, ride the train. Arms around. Choo-choo!

segments.say: Listen and move fast! Look! Stop! Come here! Go! Then, cheer for the travelers! Hooray!
segments.subtitleJa: きいて すばやく うごこう！ みて！ とまって！ こっちに きて！ いって！ それから りょこうしゃに おうえん！ ばんざい！
segments.subtitleEn: Listen and move fast! Look! Stop! Come here! Go! Then, cheer for the travelers! Hooray!

segments.say: Repeat after me. I've had the best trip ever!
segments.subtitleJa: まねして いってね。「いままでで さいこうの たびだったよ！」
segments.subtitleEn: Repeat after me. I've had the best trip ever!

segments.subtitleJa: 「いちばん よかったのは てんぼうしゃだよ。」

segments.subtitleJa: 「こんどは にじいろの れっしゃに のりたいな。」
segments.subtitleEn: Next time, I want to ride the Rainbow Train.

segments.say: Quiz time! Birimo slept on a train for the first time. What does he say? A, I've slept on a train! B, I've never slept on a train. Think!
segments.subtitleJa: クイズ！ ビリモは はじめて れっしゃで ねたよ。なんて いう？ A、れっしゃで ねたんだ！ B、れっしゃで ねた こと ないよ。かんがえて！
segments.subtitleEn: Quiz time! Birimo slept on a train for the first time. What does he say? A, I've slept on a train! B, I've never slept on a train. Think!

slide.title: Quiz
items: I've slept on a train! It was my first time!

segments.say: It's A! I've slept on a train! He did it! You did it, too. Amazing!
segments.subtitleJa: こたえは A！ れっしゃで ねたんだ！ ビリモ、できたね！ あなたも できたね。すごい！
segments.subtitleEn: It's A! I've slept on a train! He did it! You did it, too. Amazing!

slide.title: Answer
items: I've slept on a train! It was my first time!

segments.say: Bravo, travelers! You can share your best trip ever, your favorite part, and your next dream. I'm so proud of you! Next, go and talk with Birimo! Then, on to World 25, the Cave of Riddles! See you!
segments.subtitleJa: ブラボー、りょこうしゃの みんな！ さいこうの たび、いちばん よかった ところ、つぎの ゆめを はっぴょう できるね。とても ほこらしいよ！ このあと ビリモと おはなし してね！ それから ワールド25、なぞときの どうくつへ！ またね！
segments.subtitleEn: Bravo, travelers! You can share your best trip ever, your favorite part, and your next dream. I'm so proud of you! Next, go and talk with Birimo! Then, on to World 25, the Cave of Riddles! See you!
